newsitem.title: CHINA: China allows individual state debt accounts.
newsitem.headline: China allows individual state debt accounts.

text.p: China has allowed individuals to open special state debt trading accounts for the first time on a trial basis to attract more retail investors, the Shanghai Securities News said on Tuesday.
Beijing has been chosen as the test site for the personal accounts, but individuals in others parts of China will be allowed to open such accounts if the experiment succeeds, the newspaper said.

Branches of seven major Chinese brokerages in Beijing have been empowered to open the state debt trading accounts for local citizens from Tuesday, the newspaper quoted a circular from the Finance Ministry as saying.
Retail investors who open one of the new accounts will be able to trade state debt on the Shanghai stock exchange through computers in the brokerages' branches, the circular said.
The brokerages include China's giant Shenyin & Wanguo Securities, China Securities, Southern Securities, Haitong Securities and J & A securities, it said.
Individuals in China can currently only trade state debt through their stock accounts, which is both costly and inconvenient, the circular said.
The setting-up of a state debt account requires a five-yuan application fee and a deposit of at least 1,000 yuan, which amounts to one lot of state debt, it said.

"The opening of special state debt trading accounts for individuals will make it more convenient for retail investors to invest in state debt," the newspaper quoted a Finance Ministry spokesman as saying. "It will promote state debt issues and enhance the reputation of state debt."
